checks.reason: Flat area is beta0=dA/V and dd^c is Delta/(4*pi) dA, giving 4*pi*C0/V in the primitive.
A cutoff interpolation with a positive smooth constant extends the punctured radial density; its value at q is irrelevant to the measure.
Polar coordinates and t=log(1/r) give integral of t^-gamma; convergence is exactly gamma>1.
For each p>1 the pth power gives e^(2(p-1)t)t^(-p*gamma), which diverges.
Upstairs absolute continuity annihilates polar sets; the accepted disk pullback argument gives a nonpluripolar pushforward.
Two derivatives of t^(2-gamma) give the prescribed positive density with the stated normalization.
Two derivatives of -log(t) give t^-2 with the same normalization.
The radial inward flux -Pprime/2 equals the integrated density in the shrinking disk.
The flux tends to zero for gamma>1, so the distributional primitive has no delta term.
Polynomial or logarithmic growth in t is integrable against the area factor e^-2t.
Absolute growth divided by t tends to zero in both cases gamma>1.
The cutoff is supported in the coordinate disk; extension by zero introduces only smooth annular terms.
Subtracting dd^c(c*chi*P) cancels the singular density near q and leaves -M beta0 there.
Distributional Stokes and c*F=M give integral rho beta0=0.
The accepted torus Green lemma applies to the smooth mean-zero signed density and gives smooth R.
Adding Psi and the cutoff/Green correction produces c*f beta0 plus exactly the original positive pole atoms.
Local positive Laplacians give genuine subharmonic representatives; off the finite point set the constructed formulas determine them.
The constructed potential is nontrivial, upper bounded on the compact normalization, and has finite supremum.
The finite bijective normalization and removable disk-lift argument of the preceding theorem do not require p>1.
The negative-infinite set is contained in the original finite pole set and q; its only atoms are the original ones. The remaining density has mass M.
For gamma>2, P tends to zero and chi*P+R extends continuously and boundedly on the compact torus.
The nonzero t^(2-gamma) term dominates both smooth O(r) error and every r^alpha as r tends to zero.
The preceding full-type mass and fixed atom computation force c=M/F. Restored currents differ by a harmonic distribution and canonical potentials differ by a constant.
For 1<gamma<2 the primitive tends to minus infinity as a sublinear power, and at gamma=2 as minus log t.
The correction is upper bounded globally but has no lower bound in the punctured disk, so only the upper ordinary-type inequality survives.
After smooth local primitive correction, the accepted planar ideal lemma depends only on point Lelong atoms. Every positive weight has the same atoms as Psi, including a new q with atom zero.
The accepted normalization/refinement description identifies that upstairs all-weight ideal equality with the stated resolution-ideal equivalence downstairs.
Any ordinary-type solution would have mass M, hence the same positive constant; restoring its prescribed atoms makes its current identical to the constructed one.
The L1 harmonic difference is constant on the torus, with canonical point values; its unbounded punctured residual contradicts the ordinary lower bound.
The criterion concerns this exact radial logarithmic family, arbitrary chosen q and existing finite pole type. It does not characterize all L1 data or all potentials in the resolution-ideal class.
